changes.before: Provide explicit readable light colors and a dark-preference alternative while allowing native controls to use the corresponding scheme.
changes.after: Give a panel readable light and dark colors.

before: prefers-color-scheme asks about the person’s light/dark preference. color-scheme tells the browser which scheme an element supports, helping native controls use an appropriate appearance. It does not automatically recolor every author background or text rule.

The base panel is explicitly light. The dark media branch changes both authored colors and the color-scheme value. The input keeps its native behavior. Checks verify the currently active browser preference only; this preview does not switch operating-system settings. High-contrast/forced-color mechanics are a separate topic, and meaning must not depend on color alone.
Provide explicit readable light colors and a dark-preference alternative while allowing native controls to use the corresponding scheme.
after: `prefers-color-scheme` checks whether someone prefers a light or dark appearance. A media query can change your colors to match.
`color-scheme` tells the browser which appearance an element supports. This helps built-in controls, such as inputs, match it. You still choose the text and background colors you set yourself.
Keep the input usable and the text easy to read in both appearances. The preview follows the browser's current preference; these rules do not change the device setting.

before.question: If you set only color-scheme: dark, does your explicit white author background automatically become dark?
choices: Yes; color-scheme rewrites every author declaration.
No; explicit authored colors still need appropriate rules.
before.explanation: Native scheme participation and explicit author colors are related but distinct contracts.

after.question: Does color-scheme: dark automatically replace a white background you set yourself?
choices: Yes, it rewrites every color rule
No, you still need to change your background rule
after.explanation: Color-scheme helps the browser style its controls. Your explicit background still follows your own CSS rule.
